newsitem.title: USA: U.S. March budget deficit drops to $21.32 billion.
newsitem.headline: U.S. March budget deficit drops to $21.32 billion.

text.p: The government posted a budget deficit of $21.32 billion in March, the Treasury Department said on Monday, less than half the $47.07 billion deficit posted a year earlier in March 1996.
Last month's deficit followed a $44.01 billion shortfall between the government's income and its spending during February.
Total outlays in March were $129.42 billion, down from $134.3 billion in February and down from $136.16 billion in March 1996.
Revenues from taxes, fees and other sources rose to $108.1 billion in March from $90.29 billion in February. A year earlier in March 1996, the government took in $89.09 billion of revenues.

During the first six months of fiscal 1997 that ends on Sept 30, the cumulative budget deficit dropped 13 percent to $111.28 billion from $127.71 billion in the comparable first six months of fiscal 1996.

During March, receipts from individual tax payments eased slightly to $36.43 billion from $37.4 billion in February. But corporate tax payments jumped to $18.72 billion last month from $2.24 billion in February.

Many corporations make quarterly tax payments and March marked the end of the first quarter. Tax receipts from individuals will swell in April because of the mid-month deadline for filing 1996 returns.
The Clinton administration has forecast a deficit for all of fiscal 1997 of $125.59 billion, up from a deficit in fiscal 1996 of $106.99 billion.
